content.title: How the Magic routed the Hornets and Suns outlasted the Warriors to reach the 2026 NBA Playoffs
content.text: Suns, Magic secure final postseason berths for NBA PlayoffsThe Orlando Magic secured the final playoff spot in the Eastern Conference, dominating the Charlotte Hornets 121-90. Paolo Banchero scored 25 points en route to victory, as the Magic return to the NBA Playoffs for the second consecutive season.In the Western Conference, the Phoenix Suns beat the Golden State Warriors 111-96. Jalen Green scored a game-high 36 points, guiding the Suns to victory. Phoenix will face the West No. 1 seed Oklahoma City Thunder in the first round, while Orlando plays the East No. 1 seed Detroit Pistons.Share your thoughts: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementNBA Playoffs begin tomorrow Getty ImagesWith the Play-In Tournament concluded, it’s time for the postseason festivities to begin.The NBA Playoffs are HERE. And it’s going to be incredibly exciting. Four games kick off the action tomorrow. Below are the series with their respective tip-off times (ET):(5) Raptors vs. (4) Cavaliers (1 p.m.)(6) Timberwolves vs. (3) Nuggets (3:30 p.m.)(6) Hawks vs. (3) Knicks (6 p.m.)(5) Rockets vs. (4) Lakers (8:30 p.m.)Can Warriors count on Jimmy Butler next season? Getty ImagesJimmy Butler believes he will return at some point next season but doesn’t know exactly when. Since before February’s trade deadline, the Warriors, according to a league source, have made it clear to Butler that he is part of their plans. But as the summer plays out, that will likely be tested as the Warriors try to improve their roster. Are they willing to wait for Butler’s rehab? Do they trust he will be close to the same player whenever he returns?The market for Butler won’t figure to sizzle, since he’ll be coming off an ACL injury. But he could have value as a huge expiring contract.Draymond Green's future with Warriors is cloudy Imagn ImagesDraymond Green and the Warriors powered through the awkwardness of the trade deadline, but the future remains a bit murky. He has a player option worth over $27 million for next season that he has to decide whether to pick up. If Green and the Warriors rework the deal, it could allow them a little more wiggle room this summer in regard to cap ramifications. The Warriors, according to a team source, are waiting to see first what Green decides to do with the option, but his hope remains that he will stay with the only team he’s ever known.But after a lackluster season, one in which he struggled to find consistency on the offensive end to the tune of just 8.4 points a game, his lowest output since the 2021-22 season, do they really want to bring Green back, and is he still worth the price tag it would likely cost to keep him beyond next year?He made a strong case for himself in the Warriors’ win over the Clippers. Green shut down Kawhi Leonard in the fourth quarter of an intense Play-In game that saw the Warriors rally from a double-digit fourth-quarter deficit.Both Kerr and Green — who opened up about the personal pride he feels about the standard he’s helped create — have maintained throughout the season that they’d like the 36-year-old forward to finish his career with the Warriors. But with Jonathan Kuminga’s contract gone, Green’s salary is next up as the most tradeable, which will only fuel speculation about using him in trade packages.Green is still a trusted team leader and one of the best defensive players in the game, but his contract could serve as the last opportunity the Warriors have to try to put together a package for a star. Draymond on his futureDraymond Green confirmed that he is not retiring. He also makes it clear that if the Warriors want him back, he will be back. He has a player option he has to decide whether to pick up or not — but the real question for the summer is whether the Warriors would add his salary in a deal for another star player or not.More on that in a moment...Why getting another star will be complicated for Warriors Imagn ImagesThe Warriors are used to every big name seemingly being floated in their direction. Aside from the potential renewed discussion surrounding a Giannis Antetokounmpo swap with Milwaukee, several league observers have speculated about whether longtime stars Kawhi Leonard or LeBron James would ultimately find a way to the Bay.The Warriors do not have a reasonable path to cap space, so the best they can likely do to pursue James through true free agency is the projected $15 million non-taxpayer midlevel exception. To use that, they would become hard-capped at the first apron (projected at $209 million), and it would likely require Kristaps Porziņģis leaving and/or trading Jimmy Butler. They could easily get to the $6.1 million taxpayer midlevel exception, were James willing to accept something that close to his minimum. A sign-and-trade scenario, which the Lakers would have to be incentivized to accept, would also hard-cap the Warriors at the first apron, and salaries would have to sufficiently match.Matching salaries in a trade for Leonard gets tricky because the only single salary that gets them there is Butler, whom the Clippers might not want. Outside of that, it’s potentially Draymond Green (likely picking up his player option), Moses Moody and $10 million in other salaries like Brandin Podziemski or Gui Santos.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementWill Warriors trade the farm for a star? Imagn ImagesWhile the Warriors are going to have plenty of options, one team source recently cautioned that the organization didn’t plan on dealing multiple future assets to load up on even more veterans. Plus, with their cap situation and the uncertainty surrounding Butler and Moody, it will be more difficult to make a dramatic change. Still, the Warriors have all their first-round picks and, likely, a variety of choices.The most intriguing piece remains Antetokounmpo. At 31, he fits as the type of bridge superstar who could pair next to Curry for the end of his career, then carry the mantle for the organization after the most important player in franchise history retires. The competition figures to be fierce for the Greek superstar, with other teams able to offer more in the summer. The Warriors were unsuccessful in making a major deal happen before the deadline, but they’ll continue to monitor the market and see if something opens up.Steve Kerr on his future Getty ImagesKerr says he’ll sit down with owner Joe Lacob and general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. in a “week or two” to sit down and discuss his future. Says it will be a “collaborative decision” whenever it happens. 💬 “It may still go on, it may not.”Kerr says he still enjoys coaching and leaves his future open-ended.Kerr makes it clear the Warriors job is the only one he would have next year in coaching. He’s either coming back to coach Stephen Curry and Co. or he’ll go do something else. Says being able to continue coaching Steph will be “part of the equation” as to whether he returns or not.Nowitzki's reaction to Kerr embracing starsDirk Nowitzki after Prime showed the audio of the Steve Kerr-Draymond Green-Steph Curry conversation:💬 “That made me choke up a little bit. That was a cool moment.”What Kerr said to Curry, DraymondPrime just shared audio of the conversation between Steve Kerr, Draymond Green and Steph Curry ... just minutes after airing Kerr's news conference answer about it being “none of your business.”💬 “I don't know what's going to happen next, but I love you guys to death. Thank you.”Kerr addresses late-game hug with Curry and Green Getty ImagesSteve Kerr's succinct response when asked about what happened during that three-man hug with Steph Curry and Draymond Green at the end of the game."None of your business."SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPlayoffs ins and outs compared to last yearNew West teams in (team booted):- Spurs (Grizzlies)- Trail Blazers (Clippers)- Suns (Warriors)New East teams in (team booted):- Raptors (Bucks)- Hawks (Pacers)- 76ers (Heat)More on GoodwinJalen Green was the star, but Jordan Goodwin set the tone. He had three steals in the opening minutes. He chased Stephen Curry. Actually, he did what he always does. Hustle, hound, harass. It’s not always pretty (in the first half Goodwin grabbed an offensive rebound in the lane only to throw up a shot that did not hit the rim) but what he provides is invaluable. In addition to his defense, Goodwin had 19 points, nine rebounds (four on offense), six steals and two assists — a performance that should not go overlooked.Will Steve Kerr return to Warriors next season? Getty ImagesThe signs continue to point to yes — at least for another season. Kerr, 60, still has the fire to do the job and would like to continue coaching Steph Curry, the man who helped him create the culture that produced four NBA championships. Kerr and Warriors GM Mike Dunleavy have repeatedly said throughout the season that they would discuss the future after this campaign ended. A team source reiterated the same message in recent days. Another team source highlighted the need for organizational alignment regarding the road ahead — from owner Joe Lacob on down — as an important aspect in those talks.Kerr signed a two-year, $35 million extension in 2024 that is now ending. The question is, when Kerr, Dunleavy and Lacob all sit down at some point soon, will they decide to continue the partnership that has provided so much success for the group? The odds remain strong that it will.Warriors run out of gas Imagn ImagesStephen Curry turned back time on Wednesday night against the LA Clippers and extended the Golden State Warriors' season for one more game in a vintage performance that made everybody remember just how good this team with championship mettle can still be on certain nights. In Friday night's 111-96 season-ending loss to the Phoenix Suns, Curry and the Warriors looked like exactly the kind of injury-riddled team they've been most of the season.The 38-year-old poured everything he had left into Friday's game after scoring 35 points in 36 minutes on Wednesday, but much like so many of his other teammates, he just didn't have a lot of gas left in the tank. Curry finished just 4-for-15 from the field and 3-for-9 from beyond the arc for 15 points in 35 minutes. He couldn't get much separation, as evidenced by his four turnovers, against a Suns' defense that was all over him, and even when he did, he didn't have the same type of lift he had in the last game.The Warriors were only ever going to go as far in this Play-In window as Curry would take them — and Friday night offered another reminder that even the superstar guard who creates magic at times on the floor — can't overcome every obstacle in his team's way. Suns guard Jalen Green had his most important game as a pro, scoring 36 points and setting a tone the rest of his Suns teammates followed. While Phoenix had shaky moments, Green made sure to close down any chance the Warriors had when the Suns needed a bucket, playing the role for his team that Curry has played so many times for the Warriors.Now Curry and the Warriors head into an offseason of uncertainty hoping that their star can get his ailing right knee back in order with a summer full of rehab. Curry is one of the greatest players the game has ever seen, but on Friday he couldn't summon enough of what was left after a long season to extend the Warriors' season for a couple more weeks.Suns desperately needed this Imagn ImagesIf you asked which organization needed this more – the answer was obvious. Aging Golden State would have gained little advancing to the next round, where powerful (and rested) Oklahoma City waited. Better to head home and figure out how to reload next season. Phoenix is a different story. Coming off the Kevin Durant-Bradley Beal disaster, the organization needed to win back the fanbase’s trust. The eighth seed is nothing to celebrate — and the Suns made the Play-In Tournament much more difficult than it needed to be — but reaching the playoffs was an important step. The Suns may not win a game against the Thunder. In fact, they probably will not. But as long as they don’t get embarrassed, this is something from which they can build.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementPodziemski goes down swingingA really solid game for Brandin Podziemski when his team needed him. He led the Warriors with 23 points and also had 10 rebounds, shooting 9-for-17 from the field. He also had some sloppy play, including five turnovers, but his scoring kept Golden State in this one.Hobbled Porzingis can't do enoughThe Warriors got everything they could out of Kristaps Porzingis. It still was not enough. A clearly limited Porzingis had some success attacking the points. But he finished with 11 points, three turnovers — and, most notably, the Warriors were outscored by 22 points when he was on the floor.Booker becomes a facilitator Imagn ImagesMy colleague Mike Prada raised a good point during that game — is Devin Booker fully healthy?Granted, he played pretty much the entire second half. But he played a distributor role, going just 5-for-12 from the field and failing to make a 3.Booker showed his maturity by taking on a distributor role with a game-high eight assists. But Point Book will need to reassume his leading scorer role once the playoffs begin against the Thunder.Western Conference matchupsWith the Suns' win tonight, here are the full first round matchups in the Western Conference: No. 1 Oklahoma City Thunder vs. No. 8 Phoenix SunsNo. 2 San Antonio Spurs vs. No. 7 Portland Trail BlazersNo. 3 Denver Nuggets vs. No. 6 Minnesota TimberwolvesNo. 4 Los Angeles Lakers vs. No. 5 Houston RocketsGoodwin provides massive sparkJordan Goodwin is such a fun player. He was a massive force of energy on both ends of the floor, going 7-for-11 from the field and 4-for-7 from 3. He singlehandedly accounted for six steals, just an incredibly active player making a huge difference to take down the Warriors. His 19 points sure helped, too.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementJalen Green catches fire Getty ImagesWhat a statement game from Jalen Green!The 24-year-old made a massive impact tonight, shooting an absurd 14-for-20 (and 8-for-14 from 3). His whopping 36 points led all scorers.What a confidence boost for the young guard heading into the playoffs, especially after his dissappointing postseson last year.Warriors head into offseason of questionsThe injury-marred 2025-26 Golden State Warriors season is over.Now comes an offseason full of questions — including some of the most significant crossroads since Steve Kerr took over in 2014 and kick-started a dynasty.Nick Friedell and Marcus Thompson II have the full story below.Curry can't do enough Getty Images For the second time in as many Play-In Games, Steph Curry started knocking down 3-pointers in the fourth quarter after a sluggish start, and you could feel the tension rise in the arena.This time, however, it wasn’t enough. Curry lacked his typical finishing ability around the rim as he clearly did not look 100 percent recovered from the knee injury that cost him most of the season. He still finished 3-for-10 from deep, but his 17 points were not enough to save the Warriors’ season.Leading scorersHere are tonight’s leading scorers:Brandin Podzienski, GSW: 23 points, 9-for-17 shootingJalen Green, PHX: 36 points, 14-for-20 shootingSo glad Scott Foster was there for that moment. He may have been the only official willing to eject those dudes to complete the vibes.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementTechnical foul won't follow Booker into playoffsThe good news for Devin Booker and the Suns: Technical fouls from the Play-In do not carry over into the playoffs. So that ejection can simply be remembered as a weird moment.Green's 36 points lead Phoenix as Suns clinch playoff spot Getty ImagesFINAL – Suns 111, Warriors 96It took two tries, but the Phoenix Suns survive the NBA Play-In Tournament and advance to the playoffs for a series against the Oklahoma City Thunder.Coming off a 35-point showing against Portland, Jalen Green took it to another level in a must-win contest against Golden State. Green made eight of his 14 3-point attempts – tying a season-high – and led all scorers with 36 points. His treys made a major difference. Long-range shooting was the differentiator between Golden State and Phoenix, as the Suns made seven more 3-pointers. Phoenix also led in points off turnovers, 30-10.Steph Curry made just four of his 16 field-goal attempts in a 17-point showing. After a wild finish against the Clippers, the Warriors can't summon that magic tonight.I hope you all find someone who loves you as much as Draymond Green loves playing the villain, even at this point in his career.Warriors dynasty ended in 2019.They got the 2022 title.Other six seasons: 2020 bottom out, 2 Game 7 road wins in 1st round before exiting in semifinals, and 3 Play-In Tournament exits.That moment, followed immediately by two technicals and an ejection while firing up the visiting crowd, is so Draymond.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementGreen, Booker ejectedQ4 1:04 – Suns 111, Warriors 94The game is over, but the chippiness is not.Scott Foster ejects both Draymond Green and Devin Booker from the game. Green taunts the Phoenix crowd on his way out.Oh man. That group hug between Steve Kerr, Draymond Green and Steph Curry sure looks notable...Suns' playoff trip rewards surprising seasonAs weird as it is for the Warriors to be out of the playoffs, it would have felt weirder within the context of this season if the Suns missed out. They were such a pleasant surprise all year, and those fans deserve a couple home playoff games to honor the season their team had.Goodwin closes Golden State outQ4 1:06 – Suns 110, Warriors 94This game is essentially over, thanks to Jordan Goodwin.Goodwin intercepts a pass intended for Steph Curry and takes it coast to coast for a transition bucket. On the next Suns possession, Goodwin splashes a three.You don't see that every day: A challenge that results in a flopping violation against the other team.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBless the Prime cameras for capturing Steve Kerr's exasperation at that offensive foul call. Pretty clear what he was saying; it involved a word that rhymes with luck.Redemption arc from GreenSomething to think about on Jalen Green (who is now up to 36(!) points and is 9-of-14 from 3): It's safe to assume this is personal for him, as his (big-time) struggles against the Warriors in last year's first round were a fork-in-the-road sort of moment that led to him being traded to Phoenix.The Rockets lost to Golden State without Jimmy Butler, and Green's terrible showing was widely seen as proof that they need more reliable offensive firepower on the perimeter. He's certainly looking capable of providing it tonight.Suns closing in on crucial win Imagn ImagesQ4 2:02 – Suns 105, Warriors 90This game feels close to over.Dillon Brooks misses a layup attempt but easily recovers the offensive rebound, allowing the Suns to take even more time off the clock. Possession is under review on an out-of-bounds call, but either way, the Suns have a 15-point lead with just over two minutes left.Q4 2:37 – Suns 105, Warriors 90The Warriors’ defense doesn’t account for Royce O’Neale in the right corner, and he sinks the 3-pointer. He has scored 11 points off the bench.On the Suns’ next possession, Devin Booker has an open look at a 3-pointer but passes it up to use up time.Huge swing there — a late over-the-back foul call on Draymond Green to stall a potential kickout 3, followed by a Royce O'Neale triple to put Phoenix back up 12.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementQ4 3:35 – Suns 102, Warriors 87Draymond Green picks up his fifth on a loose-ball foul on a possession the Warriors extended after multiple offensive rebounds.Royce O’Neale rubs it in with a 3-pointer on the other end, and Golden State is errant on its next two 3-point attempts.Suns lineup: Booker/Green/Goodwin/Brooks/O'Neale.Centers canceled and they aren't giving up free eats to Warriors shooters.The Warriors had 41 points in last 10 minutes of Wednesday's game at Intuit Dome. They only have 15 fourth quarter points tonight with 5:21 left and down 15.Suns boost lead to 15 points Imagn ImagesQ4 5:21 – Suns 99, Warriors 84What a stretch from the Suns!Jordan Goodwin sinks a contested corner 3-pointer, and Devin Booker builds on it with a mid-range jump shot. The Suns’ lead is back up to 15, and Steve Kerr calls timeout. Booker's emergence is especially encouraging after a quiet first three quarters.Golden State sacrificing defense for offenseYou can understand why Golden State is playing this lineup considering it needs offense. The problem: Without Draymond Green or De'Anthony Melton on the floor, there's nobody to guard Devin Booker.Green electric in the Play-In TournamentQ4 6:18 – Suns 94, Warriors 83Jalen Green’s play-in performances:Against Portland: 35 points, 14-29 FG, 2-7 3PT, 5 reboundsAgainst Golden State: 36 points, 14-20, 8-14 3 PT, 6 rebounds, 4 assistsHe’s been a HUGE part of Phoenix’s push to get into the playoffs.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementJalen Green has 36 points. The Suns have needed pretty much every single one of them.Green keeping up with Warriors' 3-point paceEight 3s:- amount Warriors made in 4th quarter Wednesday at Intuit Dome- total 3s made by Warriors tonight with 7:15 left- Jalen Green 3s vs Warriors tonightSteph Curry began the quarter at 25 minutes and has yet to come out. He played 36 minutes last night; before that, the last time he played more than 30 minutes was January 22.Devin Booker, meanwhile, has not come out in the second half and has played 36 of the game's 41 minutes.Q4 7:15 – Suns 92, Warriors 78JALEN GREEN.He’s scored the Suns’ last eight points and has recorded 36 points tonight. His eight 3-pointers tie a his season-high, and the Suns have doubled their lead on Golden State.Steph Curry has woken up. Hold onto your butts.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAnd now you really can hear the groans through the TV.Curry again from 3Q4 8:30 – Suns 87, Warriors 78Steph Curry knocks down his second 3-pointer of the quarter to cut Golden State’s deficit to seven points.We thought a Curry hot streak might be coming at some point. Can the Suns do anything to fend it off?Even through the TV, you could feel the audible groan from the crowd as Steph Curry finally hits a 3.Steve Kerr in the Warriors' huddle, as captured by Prime's cameras: "Just like the other night, it's our game."Suns hold commanding lead in points off turnovers Imagn ImagesSuns have outscored Warriors 22-5 off turnovers through 3 quartersAll five Warriors starters have multiple turnovers. Jordan Goodwin has four of Phoenix's eight steals.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCould Allen see the floor?Grayson Allen has not played a single second in this game despite being made available to play. The Suns could use his shooting to negate Golden State's gapping defense, so he must still not be healthy.Suns extend lead to 9 points entering final quarter Imagn ImagesEnd of Q3 – Suns 78, Warriors 69Jalen Green cannot be contained!Thirteen third-quarter points from Green keep the Suns comfortably ahead of the Warriors. Green has made seven 3-pointers tonight, while Golden State’s whole team has only made five. A surprising development has been how limited Devin Booker and Steph Curry. Whether due to defensive pressure or possible injuries, the two stars have 20 points combined (almost fewer than Brandin Podziemski). Curry’s struggles are shocking – 2-for-9 shooting and more turnovers and field goals.12 minutes to go in Phoenix.Prime opportunity for Booker to take command Imagn ImagesNot to sound all basketball caveman'y here, but this is when the Suns really need Devin Booker to play like the star he is. He's historically been one of the best at piling up points at the end of the third quarter. With Draymond Green out of the game, now is Booker's time to generate his own offense.An important question about Jalen GreenIs Jalen Green the best Play-In player in league history? At least one person is asking this question.The Prime Video broadcast caught not only Jalen Green’s reaction to that (correct) goaltend call on him but also a disgusted shake of a head from a certain VIP sitting courtside — Suns owner Mat Ishbia.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementJalen Green STILL has more 3s than the entire Warriors team combined with less than 15 minutes to play.Green hits from DEEPQ3 2:29 – Suns 72, Warriors 64WOAH!Jalen Green has to fire from wayyy downtown to beat the shot clock, and he drills his 28-foot 3-point attempt.That trey bumps Green up to 11 third-quarter points, and seven 3-pointers in this game. He can't help but smile after that last make.Phoenix leads 22-5 in points off turnoversQ3 3:46 – Suns 69, Warriors 58A defining storyline of this game is the Warriors’ inability to curb their turnovers.They have committed 15, and the Suns have taken advantage. Phoenix leads 22-5 on points off turnovers.Whereas it felt like the Suns should've been up more at halftime, it now feels like they should be up less. You keep waiting for the Warriors to get going. But they first need to stop tossing the ball to the other team.Curry limping through third quarter Getty ImagesSteph Curry has quite a pronounced limp with 5:30 left in third quarter.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementTurnover woes continue for Golden StateEvery member of the Warriors' starting lineup has multiple turnovers tonight.Just as we all expected, Dillon Brooks and Jalen Green are shouldering the scoring load for the Suns at a combined 9-for-17 from 3.Green hits sixth 3-pointer Getty ImagesQ3 5:51 – Suns 67, Warriors 53Make that 22 points for Jalen Green!Coming off a 35-point outburst against Portland, Green is shouldering the load again with Phoenix’s playoff hopes on the line. He has six 3-point makes, two more than all the Warriors combined.Phoenix starters in foul troubleDevin Booker has four fouls, but keep an eye on Dillon Brooks as well. He has three and just nearly picked up his fourth. Gui Santos also has three for Golden State.Booker taking a secondary role Imagn ImagesThis is the second straight game where Devin Booker has looked more spectator than driver in Phoenix's offense. I'm starting to wonder if he's not fully healthy; he did miss the Suns' last two regular-season games.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAs our discussion page has pointed out, Kristaps Porzingis clearly isn't right. He entered tonight as a game-time decision due to his ankle, and it appears to be really limiting his mobility out there. But even an extremely limited Porzingis is giving this undersized Suns team some big problems. Getty ImagesDillon Brooks turned and had some words for Steph Curry after that 3. I, for one, am shocked.Q3 7:52 – Suns 64, Warriors 53The Warriors’ utilization of Kristaps Porzingis will be fascinating in this second half.Porzingis nailed a catch-and-shoot 3-pointer with the clock expiring, then got it done down low for a post bucket. On Golden State’s next possession, Porzingis scores a third way with a trip to the free-throw line.Can KP capitalize on his size advantage against the Phoenix frontcourt?Two other developments to track: Phoenix boosting its lead to 11, and Devin Booker picking up his fourth foul.Second half underway in Suns-Warriors Getty ImagesQ3 12:00 – Suns 50, Warriors 45We are back for the final half of the NBA Play-In Tournament. The Suns built an 18-point lead through the first quarter, but the Warriors have hung around and closed to within two points during the second quarter.With the playoffs on the line, I have my eye on two guys: Steph Curry and Devin Booker. Who steps up in this big moment?How Warriors fans are feeling heading into the second halfSome cautious optimism for the Golden State supporters on our “Discuss” page as we get set for the second half.As a reminder, you can hang out there with our national NBA writer Sam Amick all game long!SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMeanwhile, back in the Magic locker room...Both Jamahl Mosley and Paolo Banchero used the word "dogfight" when asked what the upcoming Magic-Pistons playoff series will be like. They expect it to be that physical, in part because they respect the Pistons for their physicality.Green putting on a show in play-in finaleFirst half 3-point shooting tonight at Phoenix!Stephen Curry's team: 3-for-14Jalen Green by himself: 4-for-7How Warriors stayed alive Getty ImagesOne reason the Warriors are still in this?Every single one of the eight Golden State players who have seen the court in this one made it into the scoring column.Golden State’s off-ball cutting, a staple of Steve Kerr’s legendary head-coaching tenure, has been superb in this one. Four different players have multiple assists, including Steph Curry and Draymond Green.Mixed bag for BookerThe bad news for Devin Booker? His shooting continues to struggle, as he has nine points and is 0-for-3 from 3.The good news? Booker is still the straw that stirs the drink for Phoenix's offense, with a team-high three assists.Another hot start for GreenFor the second time in as many Play-In Tournament games, Jalen Green is pacing Phoenix early on offense. Green has 11 points on 5-for-8 shooting, including 4-for-7 from 3-point range — highlighted by that tough contested corner 3 just before the buzzer sounded.The question now is whether he can sustain that attack in the second half. He could not against Portland on Tuesday, a big reason why the Suns lost that one.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRocky start for StephStephen Curry started just 1-for-4 from the field and is just 2-for-6 with seven points at the intermission. Still, he did not come alive until the second half against the Clippers on Wednesday — and, oh, yeah, he’s Steph Curry.A long way to go in this one for Curry and his Warriors after a strong second quarter trimmed a 18-point Suns lead down to five at the break.Warriors fans' views on the first halfSave to say the high from Golden State’s thrilling comeback win over the Clippers on Wednesday has worn off for several Warriors fans, who are chopping it up with Sam Amick in our discuss tab as their team is in another tight one against Phoenix. Here’s what they had to say...Warriors struggling with Porzingis on the floorPorzingis looks like Celtics-Knicks tonight.Warriors outscored Suns by 11 points with Porzingis off the floor for 13:23.But in Porzingis' 10:37, Suns outscored Warriors by 16 points in the first half tonight at Phoenix.Leading scorersHere are the first-half scoring leaders for each side so far tonight...Brandin Podziemski, GSW: 12 points, 5-for-11 shootingJalen Green, PHX: 14 points, 5-for-8 shootingA snoozy first half ends with Suns clinging to a 50-45 lead. Feels like Phoenix should be up by more.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementSuns take slimmed 5-point lead into halftime Getty ImagesHALF – Suns 50, Warriors 45The Suns came into the second quarter with an 18-point lead and leave it with a slim five-point advantage.Golden State forges a major advantage down low, leading in points in the paint 28-14, and lead the Suns by five rebounds. But the Warriors’ turnovers and 3-point woes prevent them from fully staging a comeback.Jalen Green leads all scorers, including a 3-pointer with time winding down before halftime.Q2 0:43 – Suns 47, Warriors 43Golden State leads 28-14 on points in the paint, as much from opportunistic cuts as pure post dominance. That’s been a productive way to offset the Warriors’ turnover woes, and it’s a four-point game.Phoenix missing Grayson AllenSuns have really missed Grayson Allen in this second quarter. Just need one more guy who can get somewhere off the dribble and force the defense to guard him away from the basket.Phoenix offense struggling in second quarterSuns only have 12 points in the second quarter. Should have been able to run out to a big lead with Warriors' offensive struggles but have let them hang around.Warriors close deficit to 5 pointsQ2 2:40 – Suns 43, Warriors 38The Suns challenge Dillon Brooks’ offensive foul and are unsuccessful. The upheld original call keeps the play as a Phoenix turnover instead of a potential and-one opportunity. Golden State can’t capitalize on the chance, as Steph Curry misses a mid-range shot.
